designGate.prompt: Before coding, sketch how narrowing [low, high) by equal 1/26 slices encodes a string, and what decode needs besides the float. Name the interval update.

parts.title: Uniform a..z

hints.text: Each letter picks one of 26 equal subintervals of the current [low, high).
idx = ord(c)-ord('a'); low, high = low + span*idx/26, low + span*(idx+1)/26.
Return midpoint. Decode: find which subinterval contains x, emit letter, narrow, repeat length times.

probes: Why isn't the float alone enough to decode?
What happens at interval boundaries with floats?

parts.title: Weighted frequencies

hints.text: Widths proportional to weight/total instead of 1/26.
Walk letters in sorted order so encoder and decoder agree on layout.
Keep uniform encode(message) working; add optional frequencies argument.

probes: What if a letter has weight 0?

parts.title: Adaptive Laplace

hints.text: Start all a..z counts at 1. After each symbol, increment that count.
encode_adaptive and decode_adaptive must update identically.
Reuse the weighted narrow/pick helpers with a live counts dict.

probes: How would integer arithmetic coding fix float precision?

criteria: stated why length (or EOF) is required
